library_items.title: Bochner-integrable function
library_items.exact_clause: Let $(\Omega,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space and $X$ a real or complex Banach space. A strongly measurable function $f:\Omega\to X$ is **Bochner integrable** if there is a sequence of integrable $X$-valued simple functions $(s_n)$ such that $$\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_\Omega\|f-s_n\|\,d\mu=0.$$ For such a sequence define $$\int_\Omega f\,d\mu:=\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_\Omega s_n\,d\mu.$$ The displayed norm limit exists: the simple integral inequality gives $$\left\|\int s_n-\int s_m\right\|\leq\int\|s_n-s_m\|\leq\int\|s_n-f\|+\int\|f-s_m\|,$$ so the simple integrals form a Cauchy sequence, and $X$ is complete. The next theorem proves that the value is independent of the approximating sequence and characterizes existence by integrability of $\|f\|$. For $E\in\mathcal A$, write $\int_Ef\,d\mu:=\int_\Omega\mathbf1_Ef\,d\mu$ whenever this function is Bochner integrable.

library_items.title: Conditional independence given a sigma-algebra
library_items.exact_clause:
Assume the axiom of choice so that the library's conditional-expectation
classes are available. Let $Y$ and $Z$ be random elements and let
$\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal F$ be a sigma-algebra. We say that $Y$ and $Z$ are
**conditionally independent given $\mathcal G$**, and write
$Y\perp\!\!\!\perp Z\mid\mathcal G$, if for every pair of bounded measurable
real functions $f,g$,
$$ \mathbb E[f(Y)g(Z)\mid\mathcal G] =\mathbb E[f(Y)\mid\mathcal G]\, \mathbb E[g(Z)\mid\mathcal G]\quad\text{a.s.} $$
This is an equality of almost-everywhere classes and hence does not depend on
representatives.

library_items.title: Gaussian process
library_items.exact_clause:
Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. A real stochastic process
$X=(X_t)_{t\in I}$ [[def-stochastic-process-and-finite-dimensional-distributions]]
is a **Gaussian process** if, for every integer $n\ge 1$, every time list
$t_1,\ldots,t_n\in I$, and every $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in\mathbb R$, the random
variable
$$
\sum_{j=1}^n a_jX_{t_j}
$$
has a normal law $N(m,\sigma^2)$ for some $m\in\mathbb R$ and
$\sigma\ge0$. Variance zero is allowed, so constant linear combinations are
included.

library_items.title: Identical distribution and IID families
library_items.exact_clause: Let $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ be random elements with the same measurable target $(E,\mathcal E)$. They are **identically distributed** if $\mathbb P(X_i\in B)=\mathbb P(X_j\in B)$ for all $i,j\in I$ and $B\in\mathcal E$, that is, their laws in [[def-law-or-distribution-of-a-random-element]] agree. They are **independent and identically distributed (IID)** if, in addition, the whole family is independent in [[def-independent-random-elements]]. Independence means mutual independence, not merely pairwise independence. No moment assumption is part of either definition. The empty family satisfies these universal conditions vacuously.

library_items.exact_clause: Assume AC. Define $\gamma(E)=\int_E e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}\,dx$ for Borel E in $\mathbb R$. For $m\in\mathbb R$ and $\sigma\ge0$, define $N(m,\sigma^2)$ as the law of $x\mapsto m+\sigma x$ on $(\mathbb R,\mathcal B,\gamma)$. This affine map is continuous: for $\sigma$>0 choose $\delta$=$\varepsilon$/$\sigma$, and for $\sigma$=0 it is constant. Its inverse images of opens are open, so it is Borel measurable. [[lem-law-of-a-random-element-is-a-probability-measure]] makes its pushforward a probability. library_items.title: Strongly measurable Banach-valued function
library_items.exact_clause: Let $(\Omega,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space and $X$ a real or complex Banach space. A function $f:\Omega\to X$ is **strongly measurable** (or **Bochner measurable**) if there are measurable $X$-valued simple functions $s_n$ and a measurable null set $N$ such that $$\lim_{n\to\infty}\|s_n(\omega)-f(\omega)\|=0$$ for every $\omega\in\Omega\setminus N$. This is a norm-convergence condition. It is not, by definition, merely Borel measurability of $f$ or measurability of every scalar function $x^*\circ f$. Changing $f$ on a null set preserves strong measurability: enlarge $N$ by that null set and retain the same approximants.

library_items.title: Time-homogeneous Markov chain with transition kernel
library_items.exact_clause:
Assume the axiom of choice. Let $K$ be a probability kernel on $(E,\mathcal E)$,
let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P,(\mathcal F_n)_{n\ge0})$ be a filtered
probability space, and let $X=(X_n)_{n\ge0}$ be an adapted $E$-valued process.
We call $X$ a **time-homogeneous Markov chain with transition kernel $K$ relative
to $(\mathcal F_n)$** if, for every $n\ge0$ and $A\in\mathcal E$,
$$ \mathbb P(X_{n+1}\in A\mid\mathcal F_n)=K(X_n,A)\qquad\text{a.s.} $$
Here the left side is an almost-everywhere class of conditional-probability
versions. The right side is $\mathcal F_n$-measurable because
$x\mapsto K(x,A)$ is $\mathcal E$-measurable and $X_n$ is
$\mathcal F_n/\mathcal E$-measurable.

**Pages:** conjugate-families-and-posterior-prediction / conjugate-families-and-posterior-prediction-examples. **Scope:** State the sufficient exponential-family update direction: for IID data with likelihood density $h(y)\exp\{\eta(\theta)^TT(y)-A(\theta)\}$ against a declared data measure and prior density proportional to $\exp\{\eta(\theta)^T\chi-\nu A(\theta)\}$ against a declared parameter measure, update $\chi$ by $\sum_iT(y_i)$ and $\nu$ by $n$, only when the prior and posterior normalizers are finite positive. Define the proper laws used in the examples: Beta$(\alpha,\beta)$ has density $p^{\alpha-1}(1-p)^{\beta-1}/B(\alpha,\beta)$ on $(0,1)$; Gamma$(a,b)$ is shape-rate with density $b^a\lambda^{a-1}e^{-b\lambda}/\Gamma(a)$ on $(0,\infty)$; Poisson$(e\lambda)$ has mass $e^{-e\lambda}(e\lambda)^y/y!$ for $y\in\mathbb N_0$, with $e\ge0,\lambda>0$ (when $e=0$ it is concentrated at zero); Dirichlet$(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_k)$ has density $\Gamma(\sum_j\alpha_j)\prod_jp_j^{\alpha_j-1}/\prod_j\Gamma(\alpha_j)$ relative to Lebesgue measure $dp_1\cdots dp_{k-1}$ on $p_j>0,\sum_{j<k}p_j<1$, with $p_k=1-\sum_{j<k}p_j$; and Multinomial$(n,p)$ has mass $n!\prod_jp_j^{y_j}/\prod_jy_j!$ on integer counts $y_j\ge0,\sum_jy_j=n$. Require $\alpha,\beta>0$, Gamma shape/rate positive, and every Dirichlet coordinate positive. Then give exact Beta–Binomial update $\mathrm{Beta}(\alpha+y,\beta+n-y)$ for integer $0\le y\le n$; exposure-adjusted Gamma–Poisson update $\mathrm{Gamma}(a+\sum_i y_i,b+\sum_i e_i)$ for independent counts and proper prior; Normal–Normal update for independent $Y_i\sim N(\mu,\sigma^2)$, known $\sigma^2>0$, prior $\mu\sim N(\mu_0,\tau_0^2)$ with $\tau_0^2>0$, variance $V_n=(\tau_0^{-2}+n\sigma^{-2})^{-1}$ and mean $V_n(\mu_0/\tau_0^2+n\bar y/\sigma^2)$; and Dirichlet–multinomial update $\alpha_j+y_j$. Prove Dirichlet normalization by iterated Beta integrals; do not claim the converse characterization of regular exponential families. Define the reusable Gaussian conditioner: for $X\in\mathbb R^d,Y\in\mathbb R^m$ jointly Gaussian with mean $(a,b)$ and PSD block covariance $\begin{pmatrix}A&C\\C^T&B\end{pmatrix}$, if $B\succ0$ the everywhere-defined Gaussian version of $\mathcal L(X\mid Y=y)$ has mean $a+CB^{-1}(y-b)$ and PSD covariance $A-CB^{-1}C^T$; $A$ and the conditional covariance may be singular. Exclude singular-$B$ pseudoinverse formulas. **Proof route:** Likelihood-kernel multiplication, positive-parameter Beta/Gamma integrals, iterative Beta normalization, and the residual $X-a-CB^{-1}(Y-b)$, whose zero covariance with $Y$ gives independence for a jointly Gaussian vector; prove the Schur-complement covariance is PSD. **Examples:** Beta–Binomial, exposure-adjusted Gamma–Poisson, normal precision pooling, multinomial Dirichlet, Gaussian conditioning with singular state covariance and SPD observed block. **Requires:** BCS-01, BCS-02; `MSF-04` `def-likelihood-density`; `MSF-05` `def-exponential-family`; `def-real-beta-integral`, `thm-real-beta-gamma-identity`, `thm-change-of-variables-for-expectation`, `thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces`, `def-multivariate-normal-law`, `lem-characteristic-function-of-a-multivariate-normal-law`. **Sources:** Gelman et al., *Bayesian Data Analysis*, 3rd ed., §§2.1, 2.4–2.6, 3.3–3.6, App. A; Johnson, Ott & Dogucu, *Bayes Rules!*, Ch. 3 §§3.1–3.5, Ch. 5 §§5.2.1–5.2.4/5.3.1–5.3.4; Bayesian-04 Särkkä App. A. The normal-model example with a textbook arithmetic typo is not reused.

**Pages:** hierarchical-bayesian-models-and-partial-pooling / hierarchical-bayesian-models-and-partial-pooling-examples. **Scope:** On standard-Borel group and parameter spaces, define a jointly measurable hyperparameter kernel $\eta\mapsto G_\eta$ and conditional observation kernels. Given a proper hyperprior $\Pi_\eta$ and conditional independence, form $\Pi_\eta(d\eta)\prod_jG_\eta(d\theta_j)f_j(y_j\mid\theta_j)$; call its normalization a joint posterior only on an observation fibre with positive finite evidence. For known-variance normal random effects with $s_j^2>0$ and $\tau^2>0$, derive $\theta_j\mid\mu,\tau,y_j\sim N(\hat\theta_j,V_j)$ where $\hat\theta_j=(\bar y_j/s_j^2+\mu/\tau^2)/(1/s_j^2+1/\tau^2)$ and $V_j=(1/s_j^2+1/\tau^2)^{-1}$. This is conditional shrinkage; when hyperparameters are unknown, integrate their joint posterior rather than plug them in silently. Define current-group prediction by integrating over that group’s posterior and new-group prediction by first drawing $\theta_{new}\sim G_\eta$ and integrating over the posterior of $(\eta,\theta_{new})$. Finite exchangeability is a modeling assumption and does not imply a mixture-of-iid representation; no de Finetti theorem is claimed here. **Proof route:** Product-kernel factorization and BCS-03 Normal–Normal update conditional on hyperparameters; check posterior normalizer. **Examples:** complete/no/partial pooling; full posterior versus plug-in hyperparameters; improper variance hyperprior causing impropriety. **Requires:** BCS-01, BCS-02, BCS-03; `MSF-01` `def-parametric-statistical-model`, `def-parameter-measurable-statistical-model-as-markov-kernel`; `def-conditional-independence-given-a-sigma-algebra`, `thm-independent-random-elements-have-product-joint-law`, `thm-existence-of-regular-conditional-distributions-for-standard-borel-targets`, `thm-conditional-integration-through-a-regular-conditional-law`. **Sources:** Gelman et al., *Bayesian Data Analysis*, §§5.1–5.4, 5.7; Johnson, Ott & Dogucu, *Bayes Rules!*, Chs. 15–16. Improper scale-prior examples are warnings, not generic prior recommendations.

**Pages:** marginal-likelihoods-bayes-factors-and-empirical-bayes / marginal-likelihoods-bayes-factors-and-empirical-bayes-examples. **Scope:** For each model with proper parameter prior define evidence $m_i(y)=\int f_i(y\mid\theta_i)\Pi_i(d\theta_i)$ using a jointly measurable likelihood kernel and a common data dominating measure. For finite model space and positive prior model weights $w_i$ summing to one, when every evidence is finite positive prove $P(M_i\mid y)=w_im_i(y)/\sum_jw_jm_j(y)$ and posterior odds equal prior odds times $BF_{21}=m_2/m_1$. A point null needs positive prior mass/explicit model atom; a purely continuous prior assigns it zero. Arbitrarily scaled improper priors do not define generic evidence or Bayes factors. Define Type-II maximum marginal likelihood $\hat\eta(y)\in\arg\max_\eta m(y\mid\eta)$ only when that maximizer exists, and define the plug-in posterior $\Pi(d\theta\mid y,\hat\eta(y))$; contrast with full Bayes retaining hyperparameter uncertainty/cross-group dependence. State no generic EB risk, consistency, dominance or credible-coverage guarantee. For the balanced one-way normal random-effects model $Y_{ij}=\mu+a_i+\epsilon_{ij}$, $i=1,\ldots,k$, $j=1,\ldots,r$, with $k,r\ge2$, independent $a_i\sim N(0,\tau^2)$ and $\epsilon_{ij}\sim N(0,\sigma^2)$, define $MSB=\frac{r}{k-1}\sum_i(\bar Y_{i\cdot}-\bar Y_{\cdot\cdot})^2$ and $MSW=\frac1{k(r-1)}\sum_{i,j}(Y_{ij}-\bar Y_{i\cdot})^2$. Then $E(MSB)=\sigma^2+r\tau^2$, $E(MSW)=\sigma^2$, so the method-of-moments estimate is $(MSB-MSW)/r$; it may be negative, and truncating at zero changes the method and does not prove a structural zero. **Proof route:** Integrate under proper within-model prior and apply finite Bayes to model indicator; derive the ANOVA expectations under the stated normal model; use BCS-05 hierarchical posterior for full Bayes and distinguish plug-in. Normalize every evidence first. **Examples:** point-null model indicator; diffuse-prior sensitivity; improper-prior arbitrary constant; negative ANOVA moment estimate. **Requires:** BCS-02, BCS-05; `MSF-01` `def-statistical-experiment`; `MSF-04` `def-dominated-statistical-experiment`, `def-likelihood-density`; `thm-bayes-formula-for-dominated-kernels`; `thm-finite-bayes-theorem`. **Sources:** Gelman et al., *Bayesian Data Analysis*, §7.4, §§5.1, 5.3–5.4; Johnson, Ott & Dogucu, *Bayes Rules!*, Ch. 8 §§8.2.1–8.2.2. **Pages:** posterior-consistency-and-tests / posterior-consistency-and-tests-examples. **Scope:** For densities against a common dominating measure define root-L2 Hellinger distance $h^2(P,Q)=\int(\sqrt p-\sqrt q)^2d\mu$, prove invariance under change of common dominating measure, and prove $\|P-Q\|_{TV}\le h(P,Q)$ and $h(P,Q)^2\le2\|P-Q\|_{TV}$ for the library's $\sup_A|P(A)-Q(A)$ convention. For a well-specified dominated IID model with truth $P_0$, state the Schwartz consistency result on a metric-separated complement: every KL neighborhood $\{P:KL(P_0\|P)<\epsilon\}$ has positive prior mass and, for each $\eta>0$, tests of $P_0^n$ against $\{P:d(P,P_0)>\eta\}$ have summable type-I and uniform type-II errors (exponential errors are a sufficient contract); then posterior mass outside that neighborhood tends to zero almost surely. State any in-probability variant with its own test/denominator rates instead of conflating the modes. **Proof route:** Hellinger factorization and Cauchy–Schwarz; lower-bound the posterior denominator over the KL set, split the tested numerator, then use Fubini and Borel–Cantelli under the stated summability. **Examples:** identifiable finite model; identifiability without testing/support; translate an L1-distance claim by its factor of two. **Requires:** BCS-01, BCS-02; `MSF-04` `def-dominated-statistical-experiment`, `def-likelihood-density`; `MSF-21` `def-kullback-leibler-divergence`, `thm-pinsker`; `def-total-variation-distance-for-probability-laws`, `thm-bayes-formula-for-dominated-kernels`, `thm-kolmogorov-iid-l1-strong-law`. **Sources:** Ghosal–Ghosh–van der Vaart (2000), §§1–2, 7–8, Theorems 2.1, 2.4, 7.1 and 7.3 and their denominator/test proofs; Kleijn–van der Vaart (2012), §4, Lemma 4.1 and Corollary 4.2. MSF-21 is planned and supplies KL/Pinsker only if its final contracts match.

**Pages:** iid-posterior-contraction / iid-posterior-contraction-examples. **Scope:** State GGV Theorem 2.1 for dominated IID density models with $\epsilon_n\to0$, $n\epsilon_n^2\to\infty$, sieve entropy $\log D(\epsilon_n,\mathcal P_n,d)\le n\epsilon_n^2$ in the same selected metric $d$ used for the conclusion and tests. The source gives Hellinger and full density $L^1$ versions separately; an $L^2$-density version additionally needs the source's uniform density bounds. Require sieve tail $\Pi(\mathcal P_n^c)\le e^{-n\epsilon_n^2(C+4)}$, and local prior mass at least $e^{-Cn\epsilon_n^2}$ where both $-P_0\log(p/p_0)\le\epsilon_n^2$ and $P_0[\log(p/p_0)]^2\le\epsilon_n^2$. Conclude contraction outside $M\epsilon_n$ in that selected metric in $P_0^n$-probability for sufficiently large $M$; state the annular-testing Theorem 2.4 separately if included. No automatic almost-sure or minimax-optimality claim. **Proof route:** Jensen/Chebyshev denominator bound; Hellinger/TV tests, sieve-tail control and shell summation. Keep the article's L1-density “TV” convention separate from library TV. **Examples:** source-covered density rate and a sieve whose entropy or tail premise fails. **Requires:** BCS-07; `MSF-04` `def-dominated-statistical-experiment`, `def-likelihood-density`; `MSF-21` `def-kullback-leibler-divergence`, `thm-pinsker` if retained with matching hypotheses; `thm-lindeberg-levy-iid-central-limit-theorem`, `thm-kolmogorov-iid-l1-strong-law`. **Sources:** Ghosal–Ghosh–van der Vaart (2000), Theorems 2.1 and 2.4, §7 Theorems 7.1/7.3 and §8, Lemma 8.1 and complete proof units, printed pp. 503–507, 521–526, 529–530.

**Pages:** misspecified-posterior-consistency / misspecified-posterior-consistency-examples. **Scope:** For a dominated IID model with $P_0$ density $p_0$, assume a nonempty KL-minimizer set $\Theta^*=\arg\min_\theta P_0\log(p_0/p_\theta)$ with finite contrasts on the relevant set. For a selected $\theta^*\in\Theta^*$ define likelihood-tilted measures $Q_\theta(A)=P_0[(p_\theta/p_{\theta^*})1_A]$; these are likelihood-tilted nonnegative measures, not normalized probability laws; the test-integral assumptions must make the source’s $Q_\theta^n(1-\phi_n)$ quantities well-defined. State Kleijn–van der Vaart Corollary 4.2 exactly: every KL neighborhood of $\Theta^*$ has positive prior mass and, for each $\eta>0$, there are tests $\phi_n$ with $P_0^n\phi_n\to0$ and $\sup_{\theta:d(\theta,\Theta^*)>\eta}Q_\theta^n(1-\phi_n)\to0$; then posterior mass outside the $\eta$-neighborhood tends to zero $P_0$-almost surely. The test limits need not be summable in this corollary. State the compact-parameter, unique-minimizer test construction only with the source's continuity and integrability conditions: compact $\Theta$, finite likelihood-ratio means, and its stated fractional-moment continuity. Do not assert generic robustness, uniqueness, or testability on noncompact spaces. **Proof route:** Apply the source's integrated-likelihood lower bound and test-splitting lemma, which yields the a.s. result from the displayed errors tending to zero; derive exponentially small errors only for the separate compact-model sufficient test construction. **Examples:** unique and nonunique KL minimizer; distant alternatives without tests; likelihood-tilted finite measure with total mass less than one. **Requires:** BCS-07, BCS-08; `MSF-04` `def-dominated-statistical-experiment`, `def-likelihood-density`; `MSF-21` `def-kullback-leibler-divergence` if the earlier final contract matches; `thm-bayes-formula-for-dominated-kernels`, `thm-kolmogorov-iid-l1-strong-law`. **Sources:** Kleijn–van der Vaart (2012), §4 Lemma 4.1/Corollary 4.2 and §3 Theorem 3.2 proof, printed pp. 366–379.

**Pages:** gaussian-process-priors-and-posterior-laws / gaussian-process-priors-and-posterior-laws-examples. **Scope:** Reuse `def-gaussian-process`; define a Gaussian process on an arbitrary index set by its mean function $m$ and positive-semidefinite covariance kernel $k$, and use consistent Gaussian finite-dimensional laws/Kolmogorov extension to obtain only the cylinder-space process under AC. This does not assert path continuity or a tight Banach-valued prior. For finite observations $Y_i=f(x_i)+\epsilon_i$, assume $f\sim GP(m,k)$, an independent Gaussian noise vector $\epsilon\sim N(0,R)$ with $R\succeq0$, and an invertible observed covariance $K_{XX}+R\succ0$. For any finite test vector $f(X_*)$, derive posterior mean $m_*+K_{*X}(K_{XX}+R)^{-1}(y-m_X)$ and covariance $K_{**}-K_{*X}(K_{XX}+R)^{-1}K_{X*}$; the prior and conditional covariances may be singular. For noisy predictions add their declared independent noise covariance. **Proof route:** FDD consistency and extension, then BCS-03 `thm-multivariate-normal-conditional-law` by residual independence and Schur complement; implementation solves the SPD observed system without explicitly forming an inverse. **Examples:** finite regression design with nonzero prior mean, singular kernel matrix plus observation noise making the observed block SPD, singular predictive covariance, extrapolation uncertainty. **Requires:** BCS-01, BCS-02, BCS-03 `thm-multivariate-normal-conditional-law`; `def-gaussian-process`, `def-stochastic-process-and-finite-dimensional-distributions`, `thm-kolmogorov-extension-for-standard-borel-coordinate-spaces`, `def-multivariate-normal-law`, `lem-characteristic-function-of-a-multivariate-normal-law`, `thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique`, `thm-non-negative-square-root-exists-and-is-unique`. **Sources:** van der Vaart–van Zanten (2008), §1 and Gaussian process preliminaries; reuse the inspected live Gaussian-process and Kolmogorov suppliers. **Proposed result item:** `thm-finite-gaussian-process-posterior-and-predictive-laws`. The finite-regression conditioning proof is local.

**Pages:** gaussian-process-support-and-concentration / gaussian-process-support-and-concentration-examples. **Scope:** Let $B$ be a real separable Banach space and $W$ a centered tight Borel Gaussian random element with law $\mu$. Use `def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces` and `def-strongly-measurable-banach-valued-function`: since $B$ is separable and $W$ is Borel measurable, countable dense centers and measurable nearest-center cells give finite-valued simple approximants converging pointwise to $W$, so $W$ is strongly measurable. First name and prove the Fernique prerequisite: for some $a>0$, $E\exp(a\|W\|_B^2)<\infty$, hence $E\|W\|_B^2<\infty$. For each $\ell\in B^*$, $x\mapsto\ell(x)x$ preserves strong measurability and $\ell(W)$ is a scalar Gaussian with finite second moment; Cauchy–Schwarz gives $E[|\ell(W)|\|W\|_B]<\infty$. Reuse the Bochner integrability criterion to define $C:B^*\to B$ by the Bochner expectation $C\ell=E[\ell(W)W]$; the Bochner norm inequality bounds $\|C\ell\|_B$, and bounded linear maps commute with this integral. The covariance RKHS $\mathbb H$ is the completion of $C(B^*)$ under $\langle C\ell,C\ell'\rangle_{\mathbb H}=E[\ell(W)\ell'(W)]$, quotienting zero-norm functionals; the inner-product formula follows by applying the bounded functional $\ell$ to $C\ell'$ inside the Bochner integral. Name and prove the Cameron–Martin translation identity: for $h=C\ell\in\mathbb H$, $\mu_h(A):=\Pr(W+h\in A)=\int_A\exp\{\ell(x)-\frac12E[\ell(W)^2]\}\,\mu(dx)$ for Borel $A$; establish independence of the representative and equality of measures from Gaussian characteristic functions on a countable norming family. Then prove $\operatorname{supp}(\mu)=\overline{\mathbb H}^{\,B}$: use Hahn–Banach separation and $E[\ell(W)^2]=0$ for the inclusion into the closure, and prove $0\in\operatorname{supp}(\mu)$ from tightness/separability and the Gaussian difference law before applying translation equivalence for the reverse inclusion. State the separable-Banach Borell bound $\Pr(\|W\|_B>E\|W\|_B+r)\le e^{-r^2/(2\sigma_W^2)}$ for $r\ge0$ when $\sigma_W^2=\sup_{\ell\in B^*,\|\ell\|_{B^*}\le1}E[\ell(W)^2]>0$; if $\sigma_W=0$, then $W=0$ almost surely and the tail probability is zero. Define $\phi_{w_0}(\epsilon)=\inf_{\|h-w_0\|_B<\epsilon}\|h\|_{\mathbb H}^2-\log\Pr(\|W\|_B<\epsilon)$. Under $w_0\in\overline{\mathbb H}^{\,B}$, $\epsilon_n>0$, $e^{-Cn\epsilon_n^2}<1/2$ for $C>1$, and $\phi_{w_0}(\epsilon_n)\le n\epsilon_n^2$, state the source sieve: a measurable $B_n$ has $\log N(3\epsilon_n,B_n,\|\cdot\|_B)\le6Cn\epsilon_n^2$, $\Pr(W\notin B_n)\le e^{-Cn\epsilon_n^2}$, and $\Pr(\|W-w_0\|_B<2\epsilon_n)\ge e^{-n\epsilon_n^2}$. The posterior theorem additionally needs the statistical distance/KL quantities controlled by this Banach norm. **Proof route:** For the Banach covariance, construct the countable simple approximants from Borel measurability/separability, use Fernique plus Cauchy–Schwarz for integrability, and reuse the named Bochner criterion, norm inequality, and bounded-linear-map commutation suppliers rather than reproving generic integration results. Then prove the Cameron–Martin density identity by exponential Gaussian tilting and finite-dimensional characteristic functions plus measure determination. For support, use a countable norming family and Hahn–Banach for one inclusion; establish positive mass in every ball about zero using tightness, a finite cover of a positive-mass compact set, and the law of $W-W\prime$, then use the translation identity for the other inclusion. Prove Borell concentration with Gaussian isoperimetry (or an exact earlier supplier), handling the zero-variance case separately. Derive the source sieve entropy by RKHS covering/translation bounds and its tail from Borell; match all constants to the displayed source theorem. **Examples:** finite-dimensional GP versus a tight Banach Gaussian; cylinder law without Banach tightness. **Requires:** BCS-11; `def-borel-probability-law-on-a-polish-space`, `def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces`, `def-strongly-measurable-banach-valued-function`, `def-bochner-integrable-function`, `thm-bochner-integrability-criterion`, `lem-bochner-integral-norm-inequality`, `thm-bounded-linear-maps-commute-with-bochner-integration`, `thm-prokhorov-tightness-theorem-on-polish-spaces`; local `thm-fernique-integrability-for-separable-banach-gaussian-law`, `thm-cameron-martin-translation-for-separable-banach-gaussian-law`, `thm-support-of-banach-gaussian-is-closure-of-rkhs`, `thm-borell-concentration-for-separable-banach-gaussian-law`, and `thm-gaussian-concentration-sieve-bounds`. **Sources:** van der Vaart–van Zanten (2008), §1.2, Theorem 2.1 and §5 proof, printed pp. 1437–1440, 1454–1456. Their RKHS-closure identity is cited, not proved; Borell's inequality is a separate prerequisite.

**Pages:** dirichlet-process-priors-and-finite-partition-updates / dirichlet-process-priors-and-finite-partition-updates-examples. **Scope:** On a standard-Borel space $(\mathsf X,\mathcal A)$ with finite nonzero base measure $\alpha$, a Dirichlet process $G\sim DP(\alpha)$ is a measurable random element of $\mathcal P(\mathsf X)$ equipped with the evaluation sigma-algebra, whose masses on every finite measurable partition $(A_1,\ldots,A_k)$ have the Dirichlet law with parameters $(\alpha(A_j))$ after omitting zero-parameter cells (zero-base cells have mass zero almost surely). Finite-partition laws alone specify only cylinder distributions, so prove existence of a countably additive measurable random probability measure. Use the following explicit normalized-gamma construction, rather than assuming a gamma process: on $\mathsf X\times(0,\infty)$ construct a Poisson random measure with sigma-finite intensity $\alpha(dx)t^{-1}e^{-t}dt$ by partitioning the mark axis into countably many finite-intensity strips, drawing independent Poisson counts and conditionally IID atoms on each strip, and proving independent-count laws by Poisson thinning. Set $\Gamma(A)=\sum_{(x,t):x\in A}t$; prove measurable evaluations, $E\Gamma(\mathsf X)=\alpha(\mathsf X)<\infty$, and $E e^{-s\Gamma(A)}=(1+s)^{-\alpha(A)}$. Thus disjoint increments are independent Gamma$(\alpha(A),1)$ variables and the total is finite and strictly positive almost surely; on the exceptional null event assign a fixed probability measure. Then $G(A)=\Gamma(A)/\Gamma(\mathsf X)$ is a measurable countably additive random probability with the Dirichlet partition laws. Under conditionally IID observations $X_i|G\sim G$, prove kernel measurability of $x_{1:n}\mapsto DP(\alpha+\sum_i\delta_{x_i})$ on finite partition cylinders; verify its disintegration identity against data rectangles by Dirichlet–multinomial conjugacy on a common refinement, then extend by a monotone-class argument to the evaluation sigma-algebra and $\mathcal A^{\otimes n}$. It is a posterior version with predictive $P(X_{n+1}\in A|X_{1:n})=(\alpha(A)+\sum_i1_{X_i\in A})/(\alpha(\mathsf X)+n)$. A measurable $\alpha$-null data event has prior-predictive probability zero and only a version choice there; individual points having zero point-mass probability under a diffuse law does not itself make their posterior update exceptional. Do not assert a general weak-support theorem without a topology and complete prior-mass proof; process definition/update alone does not imply density consistency or contraction. **Proof route:** Reuse BCS-03's finite-dimensional Dirichlet normalization/conjugacy; locally construct the Poisson random measure strip by strip and prove the Laplace-transform/normalization/Dirichlet-law claims; verify posterior identities on refined finite partitions and extend by monotone class. **Examples:** finite partition posterior and Pólya-urn draw; an $\alpha$-null event has prior-predictive probability zero. **Requires:** BCS-01, BCS-03; `def-standard-borel-space`, `def-probability-measure`, `def-law-or-distribution-of-a-random-element`, `def-identically-distributed-and-iid-random-variables`, `thm-kolmogorov-extension-for-standard-borel-coordinate-spaces`, `thm-independent-random-elements-have-product-joint-law`, `thm-change-of-variables-for-expectation`; local `def-poisson-law` and `thm-existence-of-dirichlet-process-by-normalized-gamma-poisson-random-measure`. **Sources:** Ferguson (1973), §§3–4, Lemma 1/Definition 1/Proposition 2/Theorem 1, full source PDF pp. 212–219; the detailed finite-strip Poisson construction and its measurability/disintegration proof are supplied locally. Ghosal–van der Vaart (2007), §7 finite-dimensional DP prior-mass argument, printed pp. 713–716. The mixture-contraction result is outside this pair's claims.

**Pages:** weak-nonparametric-bernstein-von-mises / weak-nonparametric-bernstein-von-mises-examples. **Scope:** In white noise $dX^{(n)}=f_0dt+n^{-1/2}dW$, define the Hilbert space $H(\delta)=H^{-1/2,\delta}_2$ by $\|g\|_{H(\delta)}^2=\sum_l a_l^{-1}(\log a_l)^{-2\delta}\sum_k|\langle\psi_{lk},g\rangle|^2$, with $a_l=2^l$ for wavelets and $a_l=\max(2,|l|)$ for trigonometric coefficients. For wavelets with $2^l$ coefficients per level, or the trigonometric basis with bounded multiplicities, $\sum_{l,k}a_l^{-1}(\log a_l)^{-2\delta}<\infty$ exactly for $\delta>1/2$; hence white noise is a tight Borel Gaussian on $H(\delta)$ but not an $L^2$-valued Gaussian. State the weak BvM precisely: with posterior $\Pi_n=\Pi(\cdot|X^{(n)})$, efficient center $X^{(n)}$ and canonical white-noise law $N$ on $H(\delta)$, $\beta_{BL,H(\delta)}(\Pi_n\circ[f\mapsto\sqrt n(f-X^{(n)})]^{-1},N)\to0$ in $P_{f_0}^n$-probability. For the source product prior, require an $S$-regular orthonormal basis with $2^l$ coefficients at level $l$, $f=\sum_{l,k}\sigma_l\alpha_{lk}\psi_{lk}$, $\sigma_l=2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$, $\alpha>0$, and IID coefficient density $\varphi$ satisfying $\sup_x\varphi(x)<\infty$, $\inf_{|x|<\tau}\varphi(x)>0$ for some $\tau>M$, and $\int x^2\varphi(x)dx<\infty$. The series condition $\sum_{l,k}\sigma_l^2<\infty$ follows from $\sum_l2^l2^{-2l(\alpha+1/2)}<\infty$, so the prior defines an $L^2$ random element almost surely. Require $f_0\in L^2$ and $\sup_{l,k}|\langle f_0,\psi_{lk}\rangle|/\sigma_l\le M$; Theorem 9 also requires continuity of $\varphi$ at each normalized true coefficient. The source's $C^\beta$ truth and $\alpha\le\beta$ condition is one sufficient route to the coefficient bound, not an extra premise of Theorem 9. Prove weak convergence in the stated topology, not total variation over all Borel sets or an $L^2$ BvM. **Proof route:** Establish posterior second-moment contraction in $H(\delta)$, finite-dimensional posterior total-variation limits and tail tightness; give the local independent-normal non-square-summability proof for the $L^2$ limitation. **Examples:** weak negative-Sobolev limit and failure of a white-noise $L^2$ probability law. **Requires:** `def-weak-convergence-of-borel-probability-measures`, `thm-continuous-mapping-theorem`, `thm-prokhorov-tightness-theorem-on-polish-spaces`; no BCS-08 dependency is used by the source product-prior BvM route. **Sources:** Castillo–Nickl (2013), Definition 1, Condition 1, Theorems 5, 7–9 and complete proof units, §§1–3, printed pp. 2009–2017/source PDF pp. 5–29. The density assumption is boundedness plus finite second moment and local positivity (and theorem-local continuity), not a sub-Gaussian tail.

**Pages:** em-algorithm-and-latent-variable-likelihood-ascent / em-algorithm-and-latent-variable-likelihood-ascent-examples. **Scope:** For a dominated latent model with jointly measurable complete-data density $p_\theta(x,z)$ and fixed data $x$, let $m_\theta(x)=\int p_\theta(x,z)\mu(dz)$. At iterate $\theta_t$ require $0<m_{\theta_t}(x)<\infty$ and define the proper conditional density $q_t(z)=p_{\theta_t}(x,z)/m_{\theta_t}(x)$. Define $Q(\theta|\theta_t)=\int\log p_\theta(x,z)q_t(z)\mu(dz)$ and the exact M-step; allow generalized EM if it increases $Q$. For each proposed $\theta$ used in the ascent claim require $m_\theta(x)>0$, $q_t\ll p_\theta(\cdot|x)$, $\int|\log p_\theta(x,z)|q_t(z)\mu(dz)<\infty$, and finite $KL(q_t\|p_\theta(\cdot|x))$. Then prove $\log m_\theta(x)-\log m_{\theta_t}(x)=Q(\theta|\theta_t)-Q(\theta_t|\theta_t)+KL(q_t\|p_\theta(\cdot|x))$, so exact M-step or Q-ascent cannot decrease observed log likelihood. If the candidate loses support so $q_t\not\ll p_\theta(\cdot|x)$, the KL is infinite and this finite identity/ascent contract does not apply. Assert only ascent by default; sequence convergence, stationary points or global maxima need separate conditions/proofs. **Proof route:** BCS-20 KL identity and Bayes factorization on a valid evidence fiber, then compare auxiliary-function values under the stated absolute-continuity and integrability conditions. **Examples:** mixture responsibilities; GEM; two local maxima; covariance collapse with unbounded mixture likelihood; support-losing candidate parameter. **Requires:** BCS-20; BCS-02; `MSF-04` `def-likelihood-density`; `thm-conditional-density-formula`, `thm-bayes-formula-for-dominated-kernels`, `thm-conditional-expectation-exists-by-radon-nikodym`, `thm-conditional-jensen-inequality`. **Sources:** Figueiredo, §§1–4, PDF pp. 1–7; its zero-KL parameter-equality statement is not used without model identifiability. **Items:** `alg-expectation-maximization`, `thm-em-observed-log-likelihood-is-nondecreasing`, `thm-generalized-em-is-nondecreasing-under-q-ascent`, `rem-em-ascent-does-not-imply-global-optimality-or-convergence`.

**Pages:** variational-inference-and-evidence-lower-bound / variational-inference-and-evidence-lower-bound-examples. **Scope:** On a declared reference measure $\mu$, let $\gamma$ be a nonnegative measurable density with $Z=\int\gamma d\mu\in(0,\infty)$ and posterior density $\pi=\gamma/Z$. For a probability density $q$ require $q\ll\pi$ and $\int q(|\log\gamma|+|\log q|)d\mu<\infty$; define $ELBO(q)=\int q(\log\gamma-\log q)d\mu$ and prove $\log Z=ELBO(q)+KL(q\|\pi)$. Define mean-field $q(z)=\prod_jq_j(z_j)$ on a product reference space and coordinate update $q_j^*(z_j)\propto\exp(E_{q_{-j}}\log\gamma(z_j,Z_{-j}))$ only when the conditional expectation is finite for $q_j$-a.e. $z_j$, its exponential has positive finite integral, and the resulting density is an admissible member of the family. Coordinate ascent is monotone only for attained exact coordinate maximizers. State reverse-KL direction, local optima and possible dependence/variance loss; an ELBO is not a general downstream-error or calibration bound. **Proof route:** BCS-20 KL decomposition, product-density algebra and exact coordinate maximization. **Examples:** exact discrete family; correlated bivariate Gaussian under mean-field; nonexistent coordinate normalizer; q supported outside the posterior support. **Requires:** BCS-20, BCS-02; `MSF-04` `def-likelihood-density`; `thm-conditional-density-formula`, `thm-bayes-formula-for-dominated-kernels`, `thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces`, `thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces` under their hypotheses. **Sources:** Blei, Kucukelbir & McAuliffe (2017), §§1, 2.1–2.5, PDF pp. 1–11; Jordan et al. (1999), §§6.1–6.3, printed pp. 213–220, PDF pp. 31–38. Both are derivations/reviews, not generic convergence or calibration theorems. **Items:** `def-variational-family-and-elbo`, `thm-elbo-kl-decomposition`, `alg-coordinate-ascent-variational-inference`, `thm-exact-coordinate-ascent-does-not-decrease-elbo`, `cex-mean-field-variational-inference-underestimates-correlated-gaussian-variance`, `rem-high-elbo-alone-does-not-certify-posterior-calibration`.

**Pages:** laplace-approximation-and-marginal-integration / laplace-approximation-and-marginal-integration-examples. **Scope:** For $I_n=\int_Ka(\theta)e^{nh(\theta)}d\theta$ on compact measurable $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ of positive Lebesgue measure, require measurable $a\ge0$, continuous at the unique interior maximizer $\hat\theta$ with $a(\hat\theta)>0$, and integrable $a$ on $K$; require $h$ continuous on $K$, $C^3$ in a neighborhood of $\hat\theta$, $-\nabla^2h(\hat\theta)=H\succ0$, local quadratic domination $h(\theta)\le h(\hat\theta)-c\|\theta-\hat\theta\|^2$ on some ball, and a strict gap $\sup_{K\setminus B(\hat\theta,\rho)}h\le h(\hat\theta)-\eta$ for some $c,\rho,\eta>0$. Prove $I_n\sim a(\hat\theta)e^{nh(\hat\theta)}(2\pi/n)^{d/2}/\sqrt{\det H}$. Noncompact integrals need explicit integrable tail localization; no relative $O(n^{-1})$ remainder without a separate higher-order proof. Also define composite trapezoid $T_N=h[\frac12f(a)+\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}f(a+jh)+\frac12f(b)]$ with $h=(b-a)/N$, and prove for $f\in C^2[a,b]$, $|\int_a^bf-T_N|\le(b-a)h^2\|f''\|_\infty/12$. **Proof route:** Local Taylor expansion, $u=\sqrt n(\theta-\hat\theta)$, dominated convergence and off-mode exponential bound; Cholesky/spectral theorem and Gaussian integral. Derive trapezoid bound by integrating second-order interpolation remainder on each cell. **Examples:** exact Gaussian integral; boundary, multiple and singular modes; smooth one-dimensional quadrature. **Requires:** BCS-20, BCS-02; `thm-multivariable-taylor-formula-with-lagrange-remainder`, `cor-second-order-taylor-expansion-with-the-hessian`, `thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique`, `cor-real-spectral-theorem-for-self-adjoint-endomorphisms`, `thm-gaussian-integral`. **Sources:** UConn note *Laplace's Method for Integrals*, entire 8-page note (author not stated); NIST DLMF §2.3(iii), equations 2.3.13–2.3.18 and conditions (a)–(c); Driscoll–Braun, *Fundamentals of Numerical Computation*, §5.6.1, equations 5.6.1–5.6.9. **Pages:** approximate-bayesian-computation-and-simulation-based-inference / approximate-bayesian-computation-and-simulation-based-inference-examples. **Scope:** Let $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$ and $(\mathsf Y,\mathcal Y)$ be standard Borel, let $\Pi$ be a prior probability and $K(\theta,dy)$ a measurable simulator kernel, and let $S:\mathsf Y\to\mathbb R^d$ be measurable. Define the summary-predictive measure $M(d\theta,ds)=\Pi(d\theta)K(\theta,S^{-1}(ds))$. For the Euclidean norm $\|\cdot\|$ on $\mathbb R^d$, the indicator ABC target is $\Pi_\epsilon(d\theta|s_0)=M(d\theta\times B(s_0,\epsilon))/M(\Theta\times B(s_0,\epsilon))$ when its denominator is finite and positive; it is exactly the posterior under the augmented event $\|S(Y)-s_0\|\le\epsilon$. For the zero-tolerance summary posterior, assume $M(d\theta,ds)=m_\theta(s)\Pi(d\theta)ds$ with jointly measurable $m_\theta$, $0<\int m_\theta(s_0)\Pi(d\theta)<\infty$, continuity of $s\mapsto m_\theta(s)$ at $s_0$ for $\Pi$-a.e. $\theta$, and an integrable envelope $\sup_{s\in B(s_0,\epsilon_0)}m_\theta(s)\le H(\theta)$ with $\int H\,d\Pi<\infty$. Uniform Euclidean-ball averaging is an approximate identity; dominated convergence gives convergence in total variation to the summary posterior proportional to $m_\theta(s_0)\Pi(d\theta)$. Full-data posterior recovery requires a factorization-sufficient statistic in the declared dominated model: $p_\theta(y)=g(y)h_\theta(S(y))$ for a common dominating measure and measurable factors; prove the posterior equality by cancellation of $g(y)$. Full-model identifiability alone does not imply summary sufficiency. Separate finite simulation error, summary-information loss and tolerance bias. Do not claim generic coverage or a universal error rate. **Proof route:** Disintegrate the prior-simulator law using the measurable-kernel bridge; prove the approximate-identity limit using the local envelope; prove full-posterior equality from the displayed factorization. **Examples:** finite-sample sufficient summary; persistent distortion from a non-sufficient summary; vanishing acceptance rate; summary density without an integrable local envelope. **Requires:** BCS-20, BCS-01, BCS-02; `MSF-01` `def-identifiability-of-an-estimand`; `MSF-02` `def-statistic-and-estimator`; `MSF-05` `thm-full-rank-exponential-family-sufficiency` only for its full-rank exponential-family scope; `def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel`, `thm-existence-of-regular-conditional-distributions-for-standard-borel-targets`, `thm-change-of-variables-for-expectation`. General summary-sufficiency and approximate-identity results are proved locally. **Sources:** Lintusaari et al. (2017), PDF pp. 1–6, 10–23, 46–47; Fearnhead–Prangle (2012), PDF pp. 1–18, 35–38; Beaumont et al. (2002), PDF pp. 1–6; Blum (2010), PDF pp. 1–11, 20–24; Robert et al. (2011), PDF pp. 1–4. Blum's quadratic-adjustment lemma proof is in an unread supplement; Robert et al. show model-choice failure, with only a special Gibbs-field exception. **Items:** `def-approximate-bayesian-computation`, `alg-abc-rejection`, `thm-abc-rejection-target-is-tolerance-conditioned-posterior`, `thm-abc-zero-tolerance-target-is-summary-posterior-under-density-regularity`, `thm-sufficient-summary-recovers-full-posterior`, `cex-identifiable-model-with-insufficient-abc-summary`.

**Pages:** iid-monte-carlo-integration-and-error / iid-monte-carlo-integration-and-error-examples. **Scope:** For a real IID sequence $(Y_i)_{i\ge1}$ (use the library definition) with $\mu=E Y_1$, define $\bar Y_n=n^{-1}\sum_iY_i$ and, when $E Y_1^2<\infty$, $\widehat{se}_n=s_n/\sqrt n$ with $s_n^2=(n-1)^{-1}\sum_i(Y_i-\bar Y_n)^2$ for $n\ge2$. Prove $E\bar Y_n=\mu$ when $E|Y_1|<\infty$, $\operatorname{Var}(\bar Y_n)=\sigma^2/n$ when $E Y_1^2<\infty$, strong and weak consistency under the corresponding integrability, and $\sqrt n(\bar Y_n-\mu)\Rightarrow N(0,\sigma^2)$ only for $0<\sigma^2<\infty$. **Pages:** importance-sampling-and-weight-diagnostics / importance-sampling-and-weight-diagnostics-examples. **Scope:** Let $\tilde p\ge0$ be a measurable target density with $0<Z_p=\int\tilde p<\infty$, target $\pi=\tilde p/Z_p$, proposal probability density $q$, and IID draws $X_i\sim q$. For ordinary IS with known $Z_p$, require $q>0$ wherever $f\tilde p\ne0$ and $f\tilde p/q$ integrable; define $\hat\mu=n^{-1}\sum_i f(X_i)\tilde p(X_i)/(Z_pq(X_i))$, unbiased for $\pi f$, with variance/CLT only when the corresponding second moment is finite. For self-normalized IS, define weights $w_i=\tilde p(X_i)/q(X_i)$ (zero where both vanish) and $\hat\mu_{SN}=\sum_iw_if(X_i)/\sum_iw_i$; require $q>0$ $\pi$-almost everywhere, $E_qw_i=Z_p\in(0,\infty)$, and $E_q[w_i|f(X_i)|]<\infty$ for consistency. A ratio CLT/MCSE requires finite second moments of $w_i$ and $w_if(X_i)$ and follows from the bivariate IID CLT/delta method; its asymptotic variance for $\sqrt n(\hat\mu_{SN}-\pi f)$ is $Z_p^{-2}E_q[w^2(f-\pi f)^2]$. State finite-sample ratio bias. Define weight ESS $(\sum w_i)^2/\sum w_i^2$ as imbalance diagnostic only: a high value cannot certify that an unvisited target region has mass zero. **Proof route:** Radon–Nikodym change of measure; IID SLLN; for the ratio result use a two-dimensional CLT plus delta method under finite second moments and nonzero denominator mean. **Examples:** ordinary versus self-normalized weights, heavy-tail mismatch with infinite variance, missed target region despite large observed ESS. **Requires:** BCS-25; `thm-change-of-variables-for-expectation`, `thm-kolmogorov-iid-l1-strong-law`, `thm-lindeberg-levy-iid-central-limit-theorem`, `MSF-14` `thm-first-and-second-order-delta-method-for-random-vectors` only if its final hypotheses match. **Sources:** Owen, Ch. 9 §§9.1–9.3, pp. 4–13, and §9.10, pp. 25–27. Theorem 9.2 proves SNIS strong consistency, not a CLT; local ratio proof is still required.

**Pages:** general-state-mcmc-kernels-and-reversibility / general-state-mcmc-kernels-and-reversibility-examples. **Scope:** Define a probability kernel, invariant probability $\pi P=\pi$, and reversibility as symmetry of $\pi(dx)P(x,dy)$. Prove general-state detailed balance implies invariance by Tonelli. Give a symmetric-measure form of reversibility that does not require a density. The existing local detailed-balance and convergence items are countable-state results and are used only as special cases. **Proof route:** Integrate the symmetric joint measure on $A\times\mathsf X$ and use the marginal identity; retain measurability and kernel hypotheses. **Examples:** finite reversible matrix, continuous symmetric random walk, invariant but nonreversible systematic composition. **Requires:** `def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel`, `def-invariant-and-stationary-distribution-for-a-markov-kernel`, `def-time-homogeneous-markov-chain-with-transition-kernel`, `thm-chapman-kolmogorov-equations`. **Sources:** Roberts–Rosenthal (2004), §2 and local checked kernel pages; source detailed-balance proof is countable-state and the general measure proof is local.

**Pages:** metropolis-hastings-algorithm-and-invariance / metropolis-hastings-algorithm-and-invariance-examples. **Scope:** On a standard-Borel state space, let target $\pi$ be a probability and proposal $Q$ a probability kernel. Form forward flow $\mu(dx,dy)=\pi(dx)Q(x,dy)$, transpose $\mu^\top$, symmetric accepted flow $\eta=\mu\wedge\mu^\top$, and a jointly measurable Radon–Nikodym version $\alpha=d\eta/d\mu\in[0,1]$. Define $P(x,A)=\int[1_A(y)\alpha(x,y)+1_A(x)(1-\int\alpha(x,z)Q(x,dz))]Q(x,dy)$; this includes the rejected self-loop. In the common-density case the off-diagonal ratio is $\alpha(x,y)=\min\{1,\pi(y)q(x|y)/[\pi(x)q(y|x)]\}$ wherever the denominator is positive, with the flow definition fixing zero-support cases. Prove the accepted off-diagonal flow is $\eta$, hence symmetric, and target invariance follows from detailed balance. Invariance alone gives no irreducibility, uniqueness, convergence rate or CLT. **Proof route:** Construct the accepted flow as the greatest measure dominated by both forward and reverse flows, disintegrate it to a measurable acceptance kernel, and verify detailed balance including diagonal rejection mass. **Examples:** random-walk and independence proposals, proposal support failure, rejected self-transition. **Requires:** BCS-29; `def-standard-borel-space`, `def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel`, `def-invariant-and-stationary-distribution-for-a-markov-kernel`; local RN/disintegration proof. **Sources:** Owen Ch. 11 §§11.2–11.4, §§11.10–11.13; Roberts–Rosenthal (2004), §§2–3.5. Any general-state result delegated to external small-set lemmas is not imported here.

**Pages:** adaptive-mcmc-convergence-and-limitations / adaptive-mcmc-convergence-and-limitations-examples. **Scope:** Let $P_\gamma$ be fixed Markov kernels each preserving and ergodic for common target $\pi$. Define diminishing adaptation $D_n=\sup_x\|P_{\Gamma_{n+1}}(x,\cdot)-P_{\Gamma_n}(x,\cdot)\|_{TV}\to0$ in probability. Define $M_\epsilon(x,\gamma)=\inf\{m\ge1:\|P_\gamma^m(x,\cdot)-\pi\|_{TV}\le\epsilon\}$; containment is that for every $\epsilon,\delta>0$ there is $N$ with $P(M_\epsilon(X_n,\Gamma_n)\le N\mid X_0=x_*,\Gamma_0=\gamma_*)\ge1-\delta$ for all $n$. State Theorem 5: if $\sup_{x,\gamma}\|P_\gamma^{N(\epsilon)}(x,\cdot)-\pi\|_{TV}\le\epsilon$ for each $\epsilon>0$ and diminishing adaptation holds, the adaptive chain's marginal law converges to $\pi$. Separately state Theorem 13: diminishing adaptation plus containment implies the same convergence. State the precise sufficient containment route of Theorem 18: a common measurable set $C$, measurable $V\ge1$ with $\sup_CV<\infty$, constants $\delta>0,\lambda<1,b<\infty$, for each $\gamma$ a probability $\nu_\gamma$ with $P_\gamma(x,\cdot)\ge\delta\nu_\gamma(\cdot)$ for all $x\in C$, common drift $P_\gamma V\le\lambda V+b1_C$, and initial $E[V(X_0)]<\infty$. Do not claim a general adaptive CLT; diminishing adaptation alone is insufficient. **Proof route:** Use the source coupling/convergence-time argument and give counterexamples for DA-alone and strong-law overreach. **Examples:** uniformly ergodic adaptive family; loss of containment; diminishing adaptation without strong LLN. **Requires:** BCS-29, BCS-32; `def-total-variation-distance-for-probability-laws`. **Sources:** Roberts–Rosenthal (2007), “Coupling and Ergodicity of Adaptive MCMC Algorithms,” §§1–10, Theorems 5, 13, 18, 19, 23. The source gives a bounded-function WLLN under its stronger theorem conditions but no general adaptive CLT.

**Pages:** state-space-filtering-and-predictive-laws / state-space-filtering-and-predictive-laws-examples. **Scope:** Reuse the exact Cat2 finite-horizon standard-Borel model: spaces $E_0,\ldots,E_T$ and $F_1,\ldots,F_T$, initial probability $\mu_0$, jointly measurable transition kernels $K_t(x_{t-1},dx_t)$ and observation kernels $G_t(x_t,dy_t)$, with joint law $\mu_0(dx_0)\prod_{t=1}^TK_t(x_{t-1},dx_t)G_t(x_t,dy_t)$. Define filtering laws $\mathcal L(X_t|Y_{1:t})$, predictive laws before observing $Y_t$, and full finite-horizon path smoothing $\mathcal L(X_{0:T}|Y_{1:T})$ as RCDs. For density updates require jointly measurable observation densities against sigma-finite measures and normalize only when each evidence is finite positive; zero/infinite fibers use the conditional-kernel filler, not division by zero. **Proof route:** Ionescu–Tulcea for the finite joint path, then RCD/conditional integration and dominated Bayes formula at each update. **Examples:** finite HMM, scalar Gaussian model, impossible observation event. **Requires:** BCS-01, BCS-02; `MSF-01` `def-parametric-statistical-model`; `SME-44` `def-general-state-space-model-by-kernels`; `thm-ionescu-tulcea-construction-of-a-markov-chain`, `thm-existence-of-regular-conditional-distributions-for-standard-borel-targets`, `thm-conditional-integration-through-a-regular-conditional-law`, `thm-bayes-formula-for-dominated-kernels`. **Sources:** Särkkä, *Bayesian Filtering and Smoothing*, Ch. 3.6 and Ch. 4; Doucet–Johansen §§2–3.

**Pages:** kalman-filtering / kalman-filtering-examples. **Scope:** Under exact SME-44 linear-Gaussian contract $x_0\sim N(m_0,P_0)$, $x_k=F_kx_{k-1}+q_k$, $y_k=H_kx_k+r_k$, centered mutually independent Gaussian initial/process/measurement noises across times, and positive-definite innovation covariance $S_k=H_kP_{k|k-1}H_k^T+R_k$ wherever inverted, define prediction $m_{k|k-1}=F_km_{k-1|k-1}$, $P_{k|k-1}=F_kP_{k-1|k-1}F_k^T+Q_k$, innovation $v_k=y_k-H_km_{k|k-1}$, gain $K_k=P_{k|k-1}H_k^TS_k^{-1}$, and update $m_{k|k}=m_{k|k-1}+K_kv_k$, $P_{k|k}=P_{k|k-1}-K_kS_kK_k^T$ (or Joseph form $P_{k|k}=(I-K_kH_k)P_{k|k-1}(I-K_kH_k)^T+K_kR_kK_k^T$). Initial, process and state covariance may be PSD; SME-44 noise covariances $P_0,Q_k,R_k$ are PSD; only observed innovation block is SPD. **Proof route:** Affine-Gaussian prediction and BCS-03 `thm-multivariate-normal-conditional-law` on a joint-PSD state/observation block; Cholesky solve implementation should not explicitly form an inverse. **Examples:** scalar update and singular prior covariance with positive observation noise. **Requires:** BCS-38, BCS-03 `thm-multivariate-normal-conditional-law`; `SME-44` `def-linear-gaussian-state-space-model-with-independent-noises`; `def-multivariate-normal-law`, `thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique`, `thm-non-negative-square-root-exists-and-is-unique`. **Sources:** Särkkä Ch. 4 §§4.1–4.3/App. A; Law–Stuart–Zygalakis Ch. 3 §3.1. Their density derivation is narrower; local PSD/SPD block proof remains required.

**Pages:** kalman-smoothing-and-rts-recursion / kalman-smoothing-and-rts-recursion-examples. **Scope:** Define fixed-interval smoothed law and RTS recursion $C_k=P_{k|k}F_k^TP_{k+1|k}^{-1}$, $m_{k|T}=m_{k|k}+C_k(m_{k+1|T}-m_{k+1|k})$, $P_{k|T}=P_{k|k}+C_k(P_{k+1|T}-P_{k+1|k})C_k^T$. Require forecast covariance $P_{k+1|k}\succ0$ wherever its inverse is used; singular forecasts require a separate range theorem, not a pseudoinverse substitution. **Proof route:** Markov factorization plus BCS-03 Gaussian conditioning and backward induction. **Examples:** two-time scalar model; singular forecast outside theorem. **Requires:** BCS-38, BCS-39, BCS-03 `thm-multivariate-normal-conditional-law`; `thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique`. **Sources:** Särkkä Ch. 8 §§8.1–8.3; Law–Stuart–Zygalakis Ch. 3 §3.1.

**Pages:** feynman-kac-particle-filters / feynman-kac-particle-filters-examples. **Scope:** On standard-Borel $\mathsf X_0,\ldots,\mathsf X_t$, define an initial probability $\mu_0$, Markov kernels $M_k$, nonnegative measurable potentials $G_k$, unnormalized path measure $\gamma_t(dx_{0:t})=\mu_0(dx_0)G_0(x_0)\prod_{k=1}^tM_k(x_{k-1},dx_k)G_k(x_k)$, and normalizer $Z_t=\gamma_t(1)$; normalize only when $0<Z_t<\infty$. For proposal initial law $
u_0$ and kernels $R_k$, require $\mu_0\ll
u_0$ and, for every $k$, $M_k(x,\cdot)\ll R_k(x,\cdot)$ for the preceding-state marginal of the proposal path law almost every $x$; choose jointly measurable versions of the kernel RN derivatives. These conditions imply $\gamma_t\ll Q_t=
u_0\prod R_k$ and give the path RN product weight $G_0(d\mu_0/d
u_0)(x_0)\prod_{k=1}^tG_k(x_k)(dM_k(x_{k-1},\cdot)/dR_k(x_{k-1},\cdot))(x_k)$. Require finite normalizer and the integrability needed for each displayed expectation. Define the $N$-particle algorithm: draw initial particles from $
u_0$ and weight them; at each time draw ancestor indices conditionally IID from normalized weights, propagate with $R_k$, and assign the incremental RN weights; report the empirical weighted measure and product-of-average-weights normalizer estimate. Bootstrap filtering is $
u_0=\mu_0,R_k=M_k$, so only potentials remain as weights. Define offspring sampling separately (multinomial or residual); prove normalizer unbiasedness by conditional-expectation induction only for this exact finite-horizon scheme and integrable weights. **Proof route:** RN path importance ratio, Feynman–Kac recursion, conditional-expectation induction; prove support/integrability before any unbiasedness claim. **Examples:** bootstrap versus informed proposal; missing support; multinomial versus residual resampling. **Requires:** BCS-38, BCS-28 ordinary importance sampling; `def-standard-borel-space`, `def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel`, `thm-measurability-of-integration-against-a-kernel`, `thm-conditional-expectation-exists-by-radon-nikodym`. **Sources:** Doucet–Johansen §§3–4; Chopin §§2.1–2.2.

**Pages:** resampling-algorithms-and-sampling-units / resampling-algorithms-and-sampling-units-examples. **Scope:** For observed units $Z_1,\ldots,Z_n$, define empirical law $P_n=n^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{Z_i}$ and the size-$n$ bootstrap as conditionally IID draws from $P_n$. For $1\le d<n$, define delete-$d$ replicates $\hat\theta_{(-I)}=T((Z_i)_{i\notin I})$ for each $d$-subset $I\subset\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and their uniform average; any variance scaling is a separate statistic with an explicit target, not implicit in the word jackknife. For $1\le b<n$, define subsampling by drawing a uniformly selected $b$-subset without replacement and applying the declared statistic at that subsample size. A sampling unit is the indivisible random/design unit used in the original experiment (individual, pair, cluster, block, or assignment unit); the resampling unit must preserve the design dependence relevant to the target. These procedures are algorithms only; validity requires a separate theorem matched to the data-generating/sampling design. Distinguish bootstrap conditional law, Bayesian posterior and design-randomization law. **Proof route:** Empirical law is a probability measure and resampling draws are conditionally IID; deletion/subsampling are finite combinatorial laws. **Examples:** IID sample mean; cluster unit; dependent time series destroyed by pointwise resampling. **Requires:** `MSF-01` `def-statistical-experiment`, `MSF-02` `def-statistic-and-estimator`; `SME-12` only for design-based assignment examples; `def-identically-distributed-and-iid-random-variables`, `def-partial-sums-and-sample-means`. **Sources:** Efron & Tibshirani (1985), §§1–2, 10, printed pp. 1–35; Bickel, Götze & van Zwet (1997), §§1–3, pp. 1–14.

**Pages:** iid-bootstrap-and-jackknife-validity / iid-bootstrap-and-jackknife-validity-examples. **Scope:** For IID Euclidean observations and finite-dimensional smooth functional such as $g(EX)$, state finite covariance, differentiability and nonzero finite asymptotic variance. Prove conditional weak consistency with exact centering/scaling and a delete-one jackknife first-order linearization. Define percentile/basic/BC/BCa/bootstrap-$t$ intervals as algorithms, but do not import a coverage theorem from the review; any later interval theorem needs its own full Edgeworth/smoothness/moment proof. **Proof route:** Existing IID CLT, local conditional CLT for empirical draws, delta method and conditional CMT/Slutsky; expose remainder $o_P(n^{-1/2})$. **Examples:** smooth mean functional, kink at absolute mean zero, median with ties. **Requires:** BCS-47; `MSF-02` `def-statistic-and-estimator`, `MSF-14` `thm-first-and-second-order-delta-method-for-random-vectors`; `MSF-10` `def-confidence-set-and-coverage` only for a separately proved coverage theorem; add local `thm-conditional-iid-bootstrap-clt-for-empirical-law`. **Sources:** Efron & Tibshirani (1985), §§1–5, 7–10; Bickel et al. (1997), §§2–5 and Appendix. The review omits many technical proofs; local theorem proof required.

**Pages:** finite-group-permutation-inference / finite-group-permutation-inference-examples. **Scope:** Let a finite group $G$ act measurably on the sample space and assume the null law is invariant: $X\overset d=gX$ for every $g\in G$. For the full orbit, the nonrandomized upper-tail rank p-value $|G|^{-1}\#\{g:T(gX)\ge T(X)\}$ is super-uniform; randomizing uniformly within the tied boundary rank yields an exactly uniform null p-value. For Monte Carlo, draw $B$ transformations IID uniformly from $G$ independently of $X$ and include identity as the distinguished $(B+1)$-st transformation; use $p_+=(1+\sum_{b=1}^B1\{T(g_bX)\ge T(X)\})/(B+1)$, which is super-uniform under ties. If sampling a subset without replacement, state its uniform-subset design and the source's rank argument separately; do not transfer the with-replacement formula without proof. The uncorrected $B^{-1}\sum 1\{T(g_bX)\ge T(X)\}$ can be anti-conservative and can equal zero. Keep sharp-null assignment inference (SME-12) distinct from IID distribution-invariance permutation inference. **Proof route:** Condition on the orbit and use the group action to make the observed rank uniform up to ties; for Monte Carlo, condition on the identity-containing random transformation list and apply the exchangeable-rank argument. **Examples:** exchangeable two-sample data, ties, random transforms with/without replacement, weak-null noninvariance, zero uncorrected Monte Carlo p-value. **Requires:** `MSF-02` `def-randomized-procedure-as-a-markov-kernel`, `def-randomized-test`; `MSF-08` `def-test-size-and-power`, `thm-p-value-superuniformity`; `MSF-11` `def-finite-group-randomization-test`, `def-orbit-rank-p-value`, `thm-finite-group-randomization-validity`; `SME-12` only for assignment-randomization examples. **Sources:** Hemerik & Goeman (2018), “Exact Testing with Random Permutations,” Theorems 1–2 and Propositions 1–3 with proof, *TEST* 27, 811–825, PDF pp. 1–15.

**Pages:** asymptotically-robust-permutation-tests / asymptotically-robust-permutation-tests-examples. **Scope:** Under $P=Q$, exchangeability gives finite-sample exactness (BCS-51). For the two-sample order-$(r,r)$ U-statistic route, take independent IID $X_1,\ldots,X_m\sim P$ and $Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\sim Q$, fixed $r\le\min(m,n)$, $m/(m+n)\to p\in(0,1)$, and a measurable kernel $h$ symmetric within each block and antisymmetric when the $X$ and $Y$ blocks are exchanged. Define $U_{m,n}$ as the average of $h$ over all $\binom mr\binom nr$ index pairs and $\theta(P,Q)=E_{P^r\otimes Q^r}h$. Under weak null $\theta(P,Q)=0$, require $0<E[h^2]<\infty$ for every assignment of $P$- and $Q$-distributed arguments to the kernel positions, as in Chung–Romano Theorem 3.1. For $\bar P=pP+(1-p)Q$, define $h_{P,Q}^X(x)=\int h(x,x_2,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_r)P^{r-1}(dx_{2:r})Q^r(dy_{1:r})-\theta$ and $h_{P,Q}^Y(y)=\int h(x_1,\ldots,x_r,y,y_2,\ldots,y_r)P^r(dx_{1:r})Q^{r-1}(dy_{2:r})-\theta$, with the corresponding pooled projection $h_{\bar P}(z)=\int h(z,z_2,\ldots,z_r,z_{r+1},\ldots,z_{2r})\bar P^{2r-1}(dz_{2:2r})$; antisymmetry and equal pooled blocks give $E_{\bar P}h_{\bar P}=0$. Require positive finite $L^2(P)$, $L^2(Q)$ and $L^2(\bar P)$ norms for the respective first projections. Prove the Hoeffding decomposition, show its degenerate remainder is $o_P((m+n)^{-1/2})$ under the fixed-order second-moment premises, and derive the sampling CLT from the projected IID sums. For permutation studentization use consistent estimators $\hat\sigma_m^2\to E_P[(h_{P,Q}^X)^2]$, $\hat\sigma_n^2\to E_Q[(h_{P,Q}^Y)^2]$, and, under IID $\bar P$ samples, $\hat\sigma_m^2,\hat\sigma_n^2\to E_{\bar P}[h_{\bar P}^2]$; define $V_{m,n}=r\{\hat\sigma_m^2/m+\hat\sigma_n^2/n\}^{1/2}$ and $S_{m,n}=U_{m,n}/V_{m,n}$. The Chung–Romano theorem then gives the permutation cdf of $\sqrt m S_{m,n}$ converging uniformly in probability to $\Phi$, and the same studentized true-sampling limit follows from its projection CLT and consistent variance estimates. Mere positive kernel second moment does not exclude a degenerate first projection. Unstudentized Wilcoxon is not licensed under a weak mean/median null by the exact $P=Q$ result. **Proof route:** Chung–Romano (2011) mixture coupling, Hoeffding/Hájek projections, second-moment remainder bounds and permutation CLT, with the explicit nondegeneracy and variance-estimator consistency conditions. Do not claim the broader 2013 asymptotically-linear/k-sample theorem's proof: its main text delegates proofs to an unavailable supplement. **Examples:** same mean/unequal variance, exact versus weak null, studentized U-statistic, degenerate first projection. **Requires:** BCS-51; `MSF-02` `def-statistic-and-estimator`; `def-identically-distributed-and-iid-random-variables`, `thm-lindeberg-levy-iid-central-limit-theorem`, `thm-slutsky-for-real-random-variables`; `def-two-sample-u-statistic-parameter`, `def-two-sample-order-r-u-statistic-and-first-projections`, `lem-two-sample-u-statistic-hoeffding-decomposition`, `lem-two-sample-u-statistic-degenerate-remainder-order`, `lem-permutation-mixture-coupling-for-two-sample-u-statistics`, `lem-pooled-mixture-projection-and-variance`, and `thm-two-sample-u-statistic-projection-clt`. The listed pair-local definitions and lemmas provide the estimand, estimator, first projections, degenerate-remainder bound, mixture coupling, pooled-mixture variance and projected sampling CLT; the planned general z-estimator theorem is not the proof supplier for this route. **Sources:** Chung & Romano (2011), Stanford Technical Report 2011-09, §3.2 Theorems 3.1–3.2 and Appendix A Lemmas A.1–A.2 with proofs, full PDF pp. 1–47; Chung & Romano (2013), *Annals of Statistics* 41(2), 484–507, full main article read but proof supplement unavailable and not a proof supplier.

**Pages:** cross-validation-risk-and-model-comparison / cross-validation-risk-and-model-comparison-examples. **Scope:** For IID data $Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\sim P$, a learning rule $A_k$ mapping a size-$k$ training sample to a predictor, and loss $L$, define $R_k=E[L(A_k(Z_1,\ldots,Z_k),Z_{k+1})]$ with an independent test observation. Given a fixed partition $I_1,\ldots,I_K$ of the indices, define $\widehat R_{CV}=n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^K\sum_{i\in I_j}L(A_{n-|I_j|}(Z_{I_j^c}),Z_i)$; holdout, leave-one-out, leave-$p$-out, repeated-$K$-fold and randomized splits use their corresponding declared training sets and averaging law. The target is risk at each fold's training size, not automatically full-sample risk. Distinguish risk minimization from true-model identification; paired overlapping folds are dependent; time series need design-matched splits. State Bengio–Grandvalet's nonexistence theorem only for a universal unbiased estimator of K-fold CV variance over all distributions under its symmetric-algorithm/IID/fixed-$K$ setup; it does not exclude model-specific, asymptotic or biased estimators. **Proof route:** Source survey for method-specific regimes; prove no-universal-estimator theorem under exact setup and explain covariance terms. **Examples:** holdout training-size bias, paired model comparison, leakage from random folds, model selection versus identification. **Requires:** `MSF-02` `def-statistic-and-estimator`, `MSF-03` `def-loss-function-and-risk`; `MSF-14` `thm-first-and-second-order-delta-method-for-random-vectors` only for a separately proved asymptotic selection result. **Sources:** Arlot & Celisse (2010), *Statistics Surveys* 4, §§2–8, pp. 40–79; Bengio & Grandvalet (2004), *JMLR* 5, §§2–4/Theorem 6 proof, pp. 1089–1105. Survey's empirical recommendations are not universal theorems.

**Pages:** statistical-and-computational-error-accounting / statistical-and-computational-error-accounting-examples. **Scope:** Define explicit successive reference targets for data estimator, finite-$B$ bootstrap/permutation approximation, discretized simulation target and floating-point output. Prove pathwise triangle-inequality decomposition by adding/subtracting each target. A variance/MSE sum needs covariance terms or independence/centering; never add error variances by default. Independent randomized-QMC replicate intervals estimate computation-randomization error, not data-sampling error; deterministic QMC has no replicate error bar without randomization. **Proof route:** Exact target identity, independent-replicate sample-variance calculation, and local propagation of proved floating-point error only on its normal-range/conditioning domain. **Examples:** bootstrap finite-$B$ Monte Carlo versus sampling error; permutation p-value resolution; Euler bias versus path variance; RQMC replication; dot-product roundoff. **Requires:** BCS-25, BCS-47, BCS-51, BCS-53; `def-moments-variance-and-covariance`, `thm-factorization-of-expectations-for-independent-variables`, `thm-lindeberg-levy-iid-central-limit-theorem`, `def-standard-relative-floating-point-model-and-unit-roundoff`, `thm-floating-point-dot-product-componentwise-and-normwise-error-bounds`. **Sources:** Efron & Tibshirani (1985), §9, pp. 29–30; Owen (2019), *Monte Carlo Book: Quasi-Monte Carlo Parts*, Ch. 17 §§17.1/17.4 and end note, printed pp. 89–99, 132–134; inspected floating-point suppliers.

**Pages:** quasi-monte-carlo-discrepancy-and-rules / quasi-monte-carlo-discrepancy-and-rules-examples. **Scope:** For points $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in[0,1)^d$, define star discrepancy $D_n^*=\sup_{u\in[0,1]^d}|n^{-1}\sum_i1\{x_i\in\prod_{j=1}^d[0,u_j)\}-\prod_{j=1}^du_j|$. Define Hardy–Krause variation with the declared upper anchor $1$ as the sum, over all nonempty coordinate subsets, of the Vitali variations of the corresponding face restrictions; for smooth functions state its equivalent mixed-derivative integral formula. Define cube quadrature, digital $(t,m,d)$-nets/sequences and lattice rules with their coordinate/base conventions. State Koksma–Hlawka $|n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nf(x_i)-\int_{[0,1]^d}f|\le D_n^*V_{HK}(f)$ only for finite HK variation under that same anchor convention, and uniform-distribution convergence only for Riemann-integrable functions. Discrepancy/variation may be unknown/pessimistic; unbounded or infinite-variation integrands have no generic QMC guarantee. **Proof route:** Give local one-dimensional summation-by-parts and a multidimensional anchored-box integration-by-parts/induction proof with exact boundary convention; construction-specific rates need their own verified hypotheses/proofs. **Examples:** smooth finite-variation integral, inverse-CDF singularity, bad high-dimensional projection, net-size restrictions. **Requires:** BCS-25, BCS-54; `def-expectation-of-a-nonnegative-or-integrable-random-variable`, `thm-change-of-variables-for-expectation`, `thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces`. **Sources:** Art Owen, *Monte Carlo Book: The Quasi-Monte Carlo Parts*, Chapters 15–16, printed pp. 3–88/PDF pp. 5–90. The source cites external full proofs of Koksma–Hlawka and construction rates; local proof remains required. Author notice forbids redistribution; source is only paraphrased.

**Pages:** synthetic-likelihood-and-indirect-inference / synthetic-likelihood-and-indirect-inference-examples. **Scope:** For a declared summary vector $S(Y)\in\mathbb R^d$, define binding map $b(\theta)=E_\theta S(Y)$ and covariance $\Sigma(\theta)=\operatorname{Cov}_\theta(S(Y))$. When $\Sigma(\theta)\succ0$, the ideal Gaussian synthetic likelihood is $\varphi_d(S(y);b(\theta),\Sigma(\theta))$; distinguish it from finite-simulation plug-in means/covariances, which give a random approximation and may fail to be positive definite. Define an indirect-inference target by minimizing a declared distance between $b(\theta)$ and the observed summary (or its probability limit), with existence and tie-breaking specified; require identification by the binding map or full summary law for parameter recovery. Do not claim exact likelihood equivalence, generic consistency, BvM or coverage from Gaussian approximation. **Proof route:** Define approximation target; any consistency theorem additionally needs uniform law, unique separated target, simulation-error control and identification. **Examples:** summary map with nonunique preimage; finite-simulation covariance noise; Gaussian summary target versus true non-Gaussian law. **Requires:** BCS-20, BCS-25; `MSF-01` `def-identifiability-of-an-estimand`, `thm-identifiability-iff-constant-on-equivalence-classes`; `MSF-02` `def-statistic-and-estimator`; `MSF-04` `def-dominated-statistical-experiment`, `def-likelihood-density`; `thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique`, `thm-determinant-differential-and-jacobis-formula`. **Sources:** Ong et al. (2018), “Variational Bayes with Synthetic Likelihood,” PDF pp. 1–4; Frazier et al. (2019), “Bayesian Inference Using Synthetic Likelihood: Asymptotics and Adjustments,” *JASA* 114(527), pp. 2821–2827. The later BSL optimizer pages and online theorem proofs were not read; no BSL calibration theorem is proposed.

**Pages:** euler-maruyama-convergence / euler-maruyama-convergence-examples. **Scope:** For the strong rate, state Higham–Mao–Stuart’s exact sufficient contract: $C^1$ drift and diffusion, one-sided Lipschitz drift, globally Lipschitz diffusion, polynomial local-Lipschitz drift, and uniform finite moments of every order for the exact solution, step process, and continuous Euler–Maruyama interpolation on $[0,T]$. Under these hypotheses, $E\sup_{t\le T}|X(t)-Y(t)|^2=O(h)$, so the grid-point RMS error is $O(h^{1/2})$. A global-Lipschitz/linear-growth specialization may derive these moment premises from an initial condition with all finite moments. Do not state only $X_0\in L^2$ as sufficient for this source theorem. For weak order $1$, state the local theorem through backward Kolmogorov regularity: for the chosen bounded test function $\varphi$, require $u(t,x)=E[\varphi(X_T^{t,x})]$ to solve the backward equation and belong to $C^{2,4}$ with its time derivatives through order two and space derivatives through order four bounded by $C(1+\|x\|^q)$. As a conservative explicit sufficient moment condition for the Taylor remainder and telescoping argument, assume the exact and Euler processes have uniform moments of some order $p\ge 2q+8$ on $[0,T]$, obtained from a finite $p$th moment of $X_0$ under globally Lipschitz/linear-growth coefficients. State a sharper exponent only if separately proved. A claim that bounded $C^4$ coefficients and test function imply this $u$-regularity needs its own stochastic-flow/Kolmogorov regularity proof. For fixed $T$ and $0<h\le1$ with $T/h$ integral, Taylor-expand one Euler step in $t$ and the Gaussian state increment through cubic order; the conditional expectation of the cubic Gaussian term vanishes and the fourth-order remainder is $O(h^2)(1+\|x\|^{q+4})$, while $(\partial_t+L_t)u=0$.
